<!-- impact:shell-launch:Configurations1 -->

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows Shell Spoofing Vulnerability | [KB5099414](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-32202) | CVE-2026-32202 | Low Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Configurations1`
- Model / role: `CTConsole-A300` / `ct-imaging-workstation`
- Deployment group: `imaging-ct`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.22621.2500`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `C` | `C` | `C` |
| Product | `L` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

`HostApplication.csproj` `OutputType=WinExe`, `app.manifest` `assemblyIdentity` name `HostApplication`.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** The product is a standalone WinExe; it does not import Windows Shell COM APIs in Core or the WPF project.
- **If we install: App may break.** Shell spoofing fixes can change how Explorer resolves or presents executables and shortcuts, which can affect manual launch of `HostApplication.exe` during lab smoke.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Host Shell remains vulnerable to spoofing on the station; the bundled app binaries are unchanged if the KB is skipped.
- **Compatibility: Compatible.** `App.xaml.cs` starts a standard WPF `Application`; no Shell API coupling in source on `main`.

### Conclusions

Host Application on `main` couples to this patch class only through the cited host stack paths; installing these KBs updates Windows components and does not patch the self-contained .NET 9 runtime embedded by CI (`ci.yml` `--self-contained true`).

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

Addresses Windows Shell spoofing CVEs in host Shell components. SBOM and source scans show no Shell package reference in the product tree.

## Product Risk assessment

- **Affected functions:** Application launch as WinExe; no in-app Shell integration.
- **Hazards:** None identified for direct in-process loading of the patched component; host-level exposure remains if skipped.
- **Install vs skip:** Install may require reboot and regression of WPF/layout or notes smoke; skip leaves host CVE exposure without changing bundled exe bits.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `None. No documented test covers Shell launch.`

### Gap Analysis

- No UI automation for WPF layout/DPI; manual smoke on `Configurations1` after host patch if installed.

## Recommendation

Hold/low priority (`Low Prio`) per FindUpdates `do_not_install`; document that skipping does not block the self-contained product exe from starting.
